state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you walk me through your thought process when you arrived at \(2n+(2m+1)=2(n+m)+1\)? How does this relate to the concept of even numbers?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, well I thought 2n was just a number, and then I added 2m+1 which is odd, so I wasn't really sure what I was doing... I just kind of combined them together. But now you're asking me about it, I'm confused - does 2n actually mean something specific about whether a number is even or odd?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of any examples where you have encountered odd and even numbers in a real-life situation? How do you differentiate between odd and even numbers in those situations?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, yeah... like if I'm counting people or things, odd numbers are like 1, 3, 5, 7 - they don't split evenly into pairs - and even numbers like 2, 4, 6, 8 can be split into two equal groups. But I'm still not getting how that connects to what 2n means... does 2n always make an even number or something?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher asks questions requiring reasoning but avoids directly addressing the 2n misconception even when the student explicitly asks about it twice, leaving the student still confused at the end despite showing some progress in understanding odd/even concepts.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student toward understanding (asking about thought process, connection to even numbers, and real-life examples) without directly providing answers, which is characteristic of Socratic method, though no counterexample is used to expose the flawed reasoning.
